journey.name: TL-13 An undo that fails leaves the task gone with no second offer
journey.description:
KNOWN-DEFECT WATCHLIST. Asserts the current behaviour; whether it is the right behaviour is a product call. See qa/TEST-PLAN.md.
Undo is the only route back from a delete and it is offered once. onUndoDelete clears the message before the call, so a restore that fails takes the offer with it: the failure is reported over the list as a plain Failure snackbar and the task is gone for good.
The 15% failure rate makes this a routine outcome rather than an exotic one - roughly one undo in seven behaves this way against the shipped defaults - which is what makes it worth pinning on a device rather than leaving to the ViewModel test that covers the same branch as state.
The delete snackbar is SnackbarDuration.Long, about ten seconds, so the broadcast has to land inside that window. Send it immediately after reading the message.
Preconditions: adb shell am force-stop com.rounds.test.to_dolist adb shell am start -n com.rounds.test.to_dolist/.MainActivity --es qa_failure_rate 0.0

actions.action: Tap the element with the content description "Delete task" on the "Book dentist" row
Verify that a message reading "Task deleted" is on screen
Using adb, break the source with `am broadcast -n com.rounds.test.to_dolist/.qa.QaControlReceiver -a com.rounds.test.to_dolist.QA_SET_FAILURE_RATE --es qa_failure_rate 1.0`
Tap the "Undo" action on that message
Verify that "No connection. Check your network and try again." is on screen
Verify that "Book dentist" is not on screen
Verify that no "Task deleted" message and no "Undo" action are on screen
Verify that exactly three elements with the content description "Delete task" are on screen
